ABSENCE: run_ensures has no RemovedInputError raise today (search_files on src/rebar/_store/ensures.py returned no matches), so this is a latent downgrade rather than an active one — but the pre-change code re-raised RemovedInputError from run_ensures unconditionally.
advisory.finding: The removed-input fail-hard guarantee is weakened for inputs that surface during run_ensures (the sweep body) rather than during path resolution: _sweep_store catches RemovedInputError and only re-raises it when running on the main thread; on the boot daemon thread it logs ERROR and continues, so a removed load-bearing input hit inside the sweep no longer aborts MCP startup.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Preserve the fail-closed disposition for a RemovedInputError raised by run_ensures during the background boot sweep (e.g., signal the main thread to exit non-zero or fail the /health probe), instead of logging it and continuing to serve.
evidence: Primary failure: a removed, still-set, load-bearing config input surfacing as RemovedInputError from inside run_ensures (an ensure unit reading a tombstoned key); RemovedInputError is a BaseException, not Exception: src/rebar/_deprecations.py:77 `class RemovedInputError(BaseException)` and tests/interfaces/contracts/test_tombstone_registry.py:73-74 assert it is not an Exception subclass.

run_ensures cannot swallow it: the per-unit handler and outer handler are both `except Exception` (src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:167 and src/rebar/_store/ensures.py:177), so RemovedInputError propagates out of run_ensures.

Old surfaced disposition: synchronous `run_startup_store_sweep()` in main() ran run_ensures on the main thread; its `except RemovedInputError: raise` guard propagated the BaseException out of main() -> process exits / MCP startup fails HARD (fail-closed). Removed call site: diff `-    run_startup_store_sweep()` in src/rebar/mcp_server.py; contract 'A removed, still-set, load-bearing input must fail MCP startup hard rather than be swallowed into a silent boot' (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:367-368).

New surfaced disposition: the sweep body runs on daemon thread 'rebar-mcp-boot-sweep' (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:315), and _sweep_store re-raises RemovedInputError only `if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:335); on the sweep thread it instead `logging.getLogger("rebar").error(...)` and returns (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:338), so the server keeps serving.

Classifier whose behavior changes: the structural fail-closed contract test_mcp_server_broad_excepts_guard_removed_input_error (tests/interfaces/contracts/test_tombstone_registry.py:291-328) requires RemovedInputError to fail the MCP server hard on the boot path; the container orchestrator/operator that previously observed a non-zero exit and withheld traffic now gets an apparently-healthy serving container.

New test only covers the synchronous (preserved) path: tests/unit/test_mcp_startup_sweep_background.py:166-184 patches rebar.config.tracker_dir, so the RemovedInputError-from-run_ensures/background-thread downgrade is unexercised.
advisory.finding: A RemovedInputError raised by an ensure unit during the boot sweep is downgraded from a hard MCP-startup abort (fail-closed) to a logged error that lets the server keep serving, because the sweep now runs on a daemon thread whose RemovedInputError handler re-raises only on the main thread.
scenarios: A crash-restarted MCP container whose store's ensure units read a tombstoned, still-set load-bearing config input: pre-change the container failed to boot (fail-closed, operator-visible); post-change it serves while logging one error line, masking the removed input.
An operator relying on process exit status to detect a removed load-bearing input no longer gets a non-zero exit from the sweep path.
advisory.suggested_fix: When _sweep_store catches a RemovedInputError off the main thread, do not merely error-log: record a fatal flag and either call os._exit/raise into the main thread via a shutdown signal, or make the /health probe report the store unhealthy, so the fail-closed contract (and test_tombstone_registry's intent) still holds when the removed input surfaces during the sweep.
